title: A wave that cannot merge should be refused at dispatch, not discovered at the gate
description:
Wave partitioning does not account for FILE OVERLAP, and the merge gate is
where that shows up — as conflicts a person has to resolve by hand, or hand to
another worker, after all the work is already done.

Observed on wave 4 of this epic, 2026-09-11. Four ticks dispatched together:
2xu, gwc, p6b, x6j. Three of them independently rewrote the SAME function,
`classify()` in internal/exec/herdr/collect.go, and the same status list in
doc.go. gwc and p6b merged with 3 conflicts; x6j then conflicted in 9 more,
across 3 files, and had to be handed to a worker (tick axq) because the
learnings rule says a union in intent is not a union in text.

This was predictable BEFORE dispatch. The tick descriptions named the files:
each of gwc, p6b and x6j said in prose that it changes what collect() decides.
Nothing checked.

`.tick/learnings.md` already carries both halves of the rule:

    Problem: Two additions to one file are a union in INTENT, not in text.
    Rule:    Hand the resolve to a worker holding the context. A versioned
             artifact has ONE owner per wave.

    Problem: One parallel tick changed a shared return shape and broke
             another's file; both green alone.
    Rule:    When parallel ticks share a contract, the merge gate is the only
             thing that tests it.

So the knowledge exists and is applied AFTER the fact. What is missing is the
check BEFORE dispatch.

What to build — decide the shape, this is not a patch:

- A tick can DECLARE the files or packages it expects to touch, and the
  orchestrator refuses to put two ticks that declare the same file in one wave.
  Cheap, mechanical, and wrong when the declaration is wrong — a worker that
  touches an undeclared file is a boundary violation the executor could report
  the way it reports the artifact boundary (tick p6b).
- Or the wave planner infers overlap from the ticks' own text and the repo,
  and warns rather than refuses. Weaker, but needs nothing from the tick author.
- Or ONE OWNER PER FILE PER WAVE is enforced the way the learnings line already
  states it: the second tick to want a file is deferred to the next wave rather
  than dispatched.

Whichever: the goal is that a wave which cannot merge is refused at DISPATCH,
when it costs nothing, rather than discovered at the gate after four workers
have each spent a few dollars and an hour.

Note the interaction with tick 5eq's declared policy: wave WIDTH is already
moving into declared policy (per-provider concurrency). Wave COMPOSITION is the
same kind of decision and probably belongs beside it.
acceptance_criteria: Two ticks that would edit the same file are not dispatched in the same wave: either the orchestrator refuses the composition, or it defers the second tick, and the chosen shape is a logged decision with its reasoning; the check runs at DISPATCH and its refusal names both ticks and the file; a tick that touches a file it did not declare is detectable after the fact rather than silent; a test drives two overlapping ticks and asserts the wave is refused or deferred.
